subject: SmartTriage integration: technical recap, PoC milestones, and SDK compatibility
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Michael Lang <michael@smarttriage.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: SmartTriage discovery — recap + proposed next steps

Hi Michael — thanks for the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed PoC plan so we can lock owners and dates. Short and practical:

Pain points you described:
- High manual triage load during peak clinic hours (30–40% longer time-to-first-response).
- Current NLU is brittle on missing context and long patient notes; false positives for urgent flags.
- Cost sensitivity: need predictable cost per encounter and ability to cap spend per clinic.

Current stack you mentioned:
- Backend: Node.js microservices behind AWS ALB
- Data: Postgres + S3 (PHI in S3 encrypted), retention policy 2 yrs
- Auth: Okta SSO, SCIM for users

Success criteria for PoC (as discussed):
1) 20% reduction in triage time on a representative workload (sample set you’ll provide)
2) End-to-end latency under 300ms p50 for single-message inference in production config
3) No PHI leaves your VPC; ability to run in Redwood Private or Dedicated (you flagged on-call isolation)

Proposed PoC / onboarding plan (owners and dates):
- Week 0 (this week): Exchange security artifacts, NDA redlines (SmartTriage legal). Owner: Michael / SmartTriage Legal
- Week 1: Provide sample anonymized dataset (SmartTriage) + acceptance test definitions (Redwood + SmartTriage)
- Week 2: Quick integration spike — SDK onboarding (we support Python and TypeScript SDKs out of the box). Owner: Sofia (SE)
- Week 3–4: Performance tuning on mirrored workload on Redwood Dedicated; share preliminary numbers. Owner: Ben (AE) + Sofia
- Week 5: Acceptance run and success criteria review; decision point. Owner: Ben / Marissa (CS)

A few clarifications / asks from our side:
- Confirm preferred SDK languages (we’ll prepare example code for Python and TypeScript).
- Which environment do you prefer for the PoC: Redwood Dedicated (recommended) or an air-gapped Private deployment?
- Please upload the sample dataset to the Drive link I’ll share; we’ll sign the DPA and send SOC2 artifacts once NDA is in place.

Attached a short Mutual Action Plan (spreadsheet) with the timeline and owners — feel free to update.

Next meeting: I’ll propose Wed next week 10–10:30am PT to review the dataset and walk through the quick SDK spike. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — excited to help reduce triage load and keep scope manageable.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachment: SmartTriage_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Michael Lang <michael@smarttriage.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: SmartTriage Legal <legal@smarttriage.io>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SmartTriage discovery — recap + proposed next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks for the succinct recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications and answers below. Quoting your summary for context.

> Success criteria for PoC (as discussed):
> 1) 20% reduction in triage time on a representative workload
> 2) End-to-end latency under 300ms p50
> 3) No PHI leaves your VPC; ability to run in Redwood Private or Dedicated

Confirming: 1 and 2 look good. For (3), we need the PoC to run in our AWS account or a Private deployment with our VPC peering — we can’t send PHI to a multi-tenant hosted endpoint.

Stack details you asked for:
- Primary services in Node.js (TypeScript), about 6 microservices.
- We have a small Go service that handles pre-processing and de-identification. If needed, we can run Redwood SDK from either Node or call a thin Python service.
- IAM: Okta + fine-grained IAM roles.
- Compliance: We’ll need to see SOC2 Type II report and the DPA (please include data retention options).

PoC timing constraints: The clinics want a pilot window in late April — ideally acceptance by 5/15 so we can plan clinician roster changes for June. That means we need the integration and acceptance run completed by mid-May.

I uploaded an initial security requirements doc here: SmartTriage_security_requirements.pdf (attached). Legal will do NDA/DPA review this week.

I’m okay with Wed 10–10:30am PT next week. Please include Ben and Marissa on the invite.

Thanks,
Michael
CTO, SmartTriage

Attachment: SmartTriage_security_requirements.pdf

Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SmartTriage discovery — recap + proposed next steps

Michael — looping in high-level commercial and a tighter PoC milestone plan so everyone has visibility.

Commercial touchpoints:
- AE (lead): Ben Carter — primary for pricing, contract, and any needed pilot credits
- SE (integration): Sofia Ivanova — hands-on for SDK support and tuning
- CS (post-acceptance): Marissa Cole — onboarding and rollout planning

Condensed PoC milestone plan (dates are target + buffer):
- Wk 0 (week of 2/23): NDA & DPA signoff (target 2/26)
- Wk 1 (week of 3/2): Dataset delivered and acceptance tests finalized
- Wk 2 (week of 3/9): Integration spike (SDK examples, quick end-to-end)
- Wk 3–4 (week of 3/16 & 3/23): Performance tuning on Dedicated; parallel security review
- Wk 6 (week of 4/6): Internal acceptance runs by SmartTriage testers
- Decision checkpoint: acceptance or iterate — ideally by 5/15 as Michael requested

SDK compatibility notes (technical):
- We will provide native Python and TypeScript SDK examples.
- For your de-id Go service, you can either: 1) call our HTTP API directly from Go, or 2) run a small Python shim that calls Redwood (we can share both examples).
- We recommend starting on Redwood Dedicated in your AWS account (Private deployment) so there’s no PHI egress; we’ll provide CloudFormation + quick-start Terraform templates.

Open items for next meeting (Wed 10–10:30 PT):
- Confirm which PoC environment (Dedicated vs Private) and who will provision the infra
- Confirm dataset drop method and technical contact for Okta/SCIM integration
- SOC2 artifacts and DPA status

I’ll prepare a brief deck for Wed showing expected perf/cost tradeoffs and a pricing estimate for the pilot. Ben

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Quick note: our infra lead prefers Dedicated in our AWS account over Private deployment for speed of setup. If you can send the CloudFormation template in advance, we’ll stand up the infra during the integration spike.

See you Wednesday.
